limitations: Shared clinical prose applies to both brothers; MRI is explicitly II-8 only. All assigned selected/alternate packet items individually compared.

patient_identity.statement: Subject II-8 matches one of the two affected Saudi Arabian brothers in Figure1 and TableS1. Packet sex and birth order agree.
limitations: Source gives current ages9and14 jointly; mapping14toII-8 and9toII-9 follows birth order rather than a separate explicitly age-labelled case paragraph.

genotype.statement: Both brothers are homozygous PI4K2A c.65C>A,p.Ser22Ter, supported by WGS and Sanger pedigree.
limitations: Source uses NM_018425 without version and hg19chr10:99400564C>A; packetNM_018425.4/hg38chr10:97640807C>A liftover/version equivalence not independently verified.

segregation.statement: Both affected brothers homozygous, asymptomatic parents heterozygous, six unaffected siblings heterozygous and II-4reference; consanguineous pedigree.

phase.statement: Homozygous single variant with both parents heterozygous supports biparental recessive inheritance; no two different alleles requiring cis/trans assignment.

causal_confidence.statement: Authors propose PI4K2A as novel recessive neurological disease gene based on segregating very early stop, shared homozygous interval and prior mouse biology.
limitations: Single related family/two affected individuals. Complete protein loss is inferred, not measured in patient RNA/protein. Prior mouse phenotype differs; no variant-specific functional assay, rescue or independent family here. High pLI is not direct recessive causal validation.

phenotype_completeness.statement: All packet items reviewed against complete clinical prose, pedigree, MRI and variant workbook. Positive shared findings mostly agree; specific negative MRI/seizure/systemic findings are unestablished.
limitations: Normal strength does not demonstrate absence of muscle atrophy; normal systemic examination does not specifically exclude recurrent infections; third-percentile growth does not establish absence of microcephaly.

assessment.statement: Homozygous c.65C>A,p.Ser22Ter agrees with the article and TableS1 PI4K2A rows.
limitations: hg38 coordinate and transcript-version normalization not independently verified from original hg19 and unversioned accession.

assessment.statement: Pes cavus explicitly present in both boys.
Both have global developmental delay with acquired-skill loss at5–6months, supporting infantile onset.
Both unable to stand or walk but able to crawl and sit unaided, supporting severe motor delay.
Both explicitly nonambulatory.
Akathisia described during the remainder of infancy and persists to current ages.
Hypoplasia of the brainstem: II-8 infant MRI caption describes callosal hypoplasia, small pons/brainstem and small mega cisterna magna; image personally inspected.
limitations: Small structures are descriptive rather than quantified hypoplasia; no independent MRI measurement.

assessment.statement: Hypoplasia of the pons: II-8 infant MRI caption describes callosal hypoplasia, small pons/brainstem and small mega cisterna magna; image personally inspected.

Complete review of main, all five PDF pages, pedigree, MRI supplement, and both workbook sheets; selectedII-8 plus alternateII-9 fully adjudicated. Scientific uncertainty remains despite complete reading.

Both share early regression and later myoclonus/seizures. MRI is II-8 only; II-9 is not assigned MRI findings. No patient-level raw images beyond the one published sagittal view, raw genome/BAM files or independent charts reviewed.

All86variant rows read, not just PI4K2A. TableS1 includes low-quality flags and synonymous/higher-frequency variants, so these rows are not identical to the13high-confidence shared coding variants described in Results. No alternative variant clinically excluded solely by this review.

Original workbook gene_symbol K46 is date-formatted1-Mar (stored date2018-03-01); adjoining transcript names MARC1. Preserved as source spreadsheet corruption, not silently corrected. H column retains a single sample-labelled AD_ALT header across both subjects; do not overinterpret as validated allele fractions.

Original workbook narrow columns clip long strings. All original views inspected, then full annotations/alleles/readme inspected in display-only reflow. Original workbook unchanged. Historical population absence not updated; protein-null assertion remains inferred. Clinical classification not independently established.
